newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cattle breeders burn Dutch, Irish veal.
newsitem.headline: French cattle breeders burn Dutch, Irish veal.

text.p: About 800 French cattle breeders ransacked Dutch and Irish trucks and burnt cargoes of veal overnight to back their demands for more European Union aid in coping with the mad cow crisis, officials said on Monday.

The breeders, mostly from western and southwestern France, seized veal carcasses from four Dutch and one Irish truck and incinerated the meat on big bonfires at the Rungis wholesale market south of Paris.

"There were no arrests and no confrontations with police," said Philippe Stisi, a spokesman for the Rungis market. He said that the breeders, who came in about 20 buses, were leaving on Monday morning.
The protesters want EU farm ministers meeting in Brussels for two days from Monday to do more to protect French breeders in the wake of the crisis over mad cow disease.

The National Bovine Federation, which organised the protest, says a package of measures agreed by EU farm ministers in October to cut beef surpluses gave breeders in nations like the Netherlands a competitive edge over their French rivals.
